chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Face the Qiblah with the underside of his feet.'
ai.seo_question: How should the feet of the deceased be oriented towards the Qiblah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific fiqh of facing the deceased toward the Qiblah by orienting the soles of the feet, a practice rooted in the desire to honor the dead as they would face the Kaaba in prayer. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ritual purity and dignity in death, linking the physical orientation of the body to the spiritual orientation of the soul toward God.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Abu Hamza, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the deceased, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Get him to face the Qiblah with the underside of his feet’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “
I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a dying person. He said, ‘Make the undersides of his feet face toward Qiblah.’ ”
